header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Exercise Patience with Illness

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Hudhayfah (RA) reports from his aunt Hadhrat Faatimah (RA) that she was with a few women who visited Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was suffering high fever. Because of the intensity of the fever, Rasulullaah ﷺ had a water bag hung overhead from a branch and lay beneath it so that drops of water fell on to his head. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" she said, "Why don't you pray to Allaah to cure you?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Those who suffer the most difficulties are the Ambiyaa, then those closest to them, then those closest to them and then those closest to them."[^1]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was once overcome with pain, he was in great suffering and turned from side to side on his bed. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked, "Would you not be angry with any of us if we had to do this?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Difficulties will continue harassing a Mu'min but whenever he is pricked by a thorn or suffers any other pain, a sin is forgiven and a stage (in the Aakhirah) is elevated."[^2]
The Sahabah (RA) Exercise Patience with Illness
The People of Quba and the Ansaar Patiently Bear Fever

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that fever (in the human form Allaah had granted it) once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Who is it?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "Ummu Mildam(1)," was the reply. Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed it to go to the people of Quba and (when it did) only Allaah knows how many people were afflicted. When the people of Quba came to complain about it to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked, "You have a choice. If you wish, I shall pray to Allaah to remove it from you or if you prefer, it could (remain amongst you and thereby) be a means of purification for you (from sin)." "Can you really do this?" they asked. When Rasulullaah ﷺ conformed that he could, they bade him to let it stay.[^3]

Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) narrates that when fever once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked who it was. It replied, "I am fever. I peel at flesh and suck blood." "Go to the people of Quba," Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed. It then proceeded there and (after a while) the people of Quba came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with pale faces. When they complained about the fever to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he asked them, "You have a choice. If you wish, I shall pray to Allaah and He will remove it from you or if you prefer, you could leave it to remain amongst you and thereby be a means of removing all the sins you may have left." Their reply was, "Why not (why should we not want our sins forgiven)? Leave it, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!"[^4]
Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.154). Ahmad and Tabraani have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.292).
Ibn Sa'd, Haakim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.154). Ahmad has reported a similar narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.292).
This is the title Arabs give to fever.
Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.260). Abu Ya'la and Ibn Hibbaan have also reported the narration.
